messages.author: 8fdb11ff9885ec5b
messages.subject: PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat Channel naming
parts:
Hello, MSstats team,

I am using MSstatsTMT and struggling to name the Channel field correctly in the annotation file and in the input data.  I am working with Protein Discoverer 2-plex.  The file is sent to me with intensities named "Abundance:  126" and "Abundance: 127" which of course I can rename to anything I choose.  Naming them anything _other_ than "Abundance..126" and "Abundance..127" results in an error that the intensity field is not present, so this is what I name them.

In the PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat function, the leading values of the field names are stripped after the input file is converted to long format, and leaves simply "126" and "127".  However using "126" and "127" as the values in the Channel field on the annotation file does not seem to work.  I have tried them as character and as factors, but I always find myself stopped at this error: 
Error in PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(testInput, annotation = testAnno, which.proteinid = "Master.Protein.Accessions",  : 
  Please check the annotation file. The channel name must be matched with that in input data

On the vignette page (http://msstats.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/MSstatsTMT-_-A-package-for-protein-significance-analysis-in-shotgun-mass-spectrometry-based-proteomic-experiments-with-tandem-mass-tag-TMT-labeling.htm) none of the intensity values start with "Abundance", and the channel fields all contain the leading X's, which somewhat baffles me reading the code. I am unsure how to reconcile what I see on the vignette with the errors that I receive running the function.

I am running R version 3.5.0 and MSstatsTMT_1.0.0.

Thank you!

Laura

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat Channel naming
parts:
Hi Laura,

Thank you for using MSstatsTMT. For your data, the correct way to use MSstatsTMT is:
  • In the annotation file, name the two channels like "126" and "127" 
  • In the PD PSM file, name the intensity columns like "Abundance..126" and "Abundance..127".
 Please let me know if it doesn't work. The vignettes in MSstats website is out of date and the correct one is shown in the bioconductor page: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/MSstatsTMT/inst/doc/MSstatsTMT.html. I'll update the MSstatsTMT webpage. 

Best,
Ting

messages.author: 8fdb11ff9885ec5b
messages.subject: Re: PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat Channel naming
parts:
Thank you Ting,

I might have figured out the problem, at least for my small data set.  I was reading in Channel as you describe for the annotation and PD PSM file.  The problem is/was that in the annotation file, the two appeared in a different order (row 1 is 126, row 2 is 127 in the annotation file, row 1 is 126 and row 2 is 126 in the PD PSM file).  That breaks the step in lines 330-333 from the function code (https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsTMT/blob/master/R/PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat.R) 

I am still running this on the *big* data set, so I am not sure if this actually fixed the problem.  It did work on the subset of data that I was playing with.

Thank you for your help,
Laura
